learning: Iterations 0 and 3 differ only in span (40 vs 60 mm) and show progress 0.664 vs 0.275, so progress appears to fall as span widens. Iteration 3 showed that kp 6 at 60 mm did not restore progress, so gain scaling alone is not the lever. If progress rises toward 0.6 with line losses near 1, span is controlling and 40 to 50 mm is the right range. If progress stays near 0.4 or below, the span effect is not monotonic and the next lever is wheel_track for max_error, applied at the 40 mm span.
notes: Narrows the span to 50 mm (12 mm footprint, y 0.05) as the Builder proposed, and sets kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.35, between the 40 mm and 60 mm gain sets. The aim is to test whether oval progress recovers toward the 40 mm level.
rationale: Iteration 0 (40 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, kp 4, ki 0.2, kd 0.3) remains the best design so far, with oval progress 0.664 and score 159.7. Iteration 3 (60 mm span, 12 mm footprint, kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45) fell to oval progress 0.275, and iteration 2 (60 mm, 16 mm, same gains) reached 0.405. The 60 mm span is therefore the likely cause of the drop, and footprint is secondary. The Builder's proposal narrows the span to 50 mm at 12 mm footprint and y 0.05, with body, wheel and mass unchanged, so that span is the only geometry variable. The controller must be matched to this geometry. Sensor weights are unchanged at (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), since the signal is a reading-weighted average and these weights already fix its scale. With a narrower span the outer sensors reach the tape edge at smaller offsets, so the signal per metre of offset is steeper than at 60 mm. Iteration 3 showed that kp 6 at 60 mm did not help progress, so I do not scale kp up. I interpolate between the best-performing gains at 40 mm (kp 4, ki 0.2, kd 0.3) and the 60 mm gains (kp 6, ki 0.3, kd 0.45), taking kp 4.5, ki 0.25, kd 0.35. This is a moderate step that stays close to the gains that gave the best progress. The lead stays at y 0.05, because iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 collapses progress. line_loss stays last_direction, since iteration 0 and 3 line-loss counts (1.25 to 1.9) were handled by that rule. base_speed 1.5 is kept, since the oval finished in 1.73 s in iteration 0, so speed is not the limit. The measurement request keeps the full set, including noise_robustness, so the result can be compared against iterations 0 to 3 on the same metrics.
